source.version_note: Published BMC Psychology 13, article 1379, DOI 10.1186/s40359-025-03655-3, 29 December 2025. The earlier PDF creation timestamp is not the publication date or proof of a correction. No separate erratum was verified.
source.verification_method: All 15 supplied pages, all 95 references, four stimulus tables and three figures read; trauma image and both path diagrams visually inspected. Invisible link-formatting characters were removed for readable reference extraction without omitting text. Crossref and publisher/PubMed metadata verify main identity and three original-source identities; original cited studies, chapter, OSF raw data/scripts and mediation analyses were not independently read/reproduced.

citation.title: Perceiving minds in machines: how perceived theory of mind in robots influences human–robot empathy through the lens of mind perception theory

reading.source_scope_note: Four Credamo vignette/image experiments with 394 retained participations manipulate descriptions of a robot’s cognitive or affective mentalizing, followed by an extreme fictional damage scenario and self-reported empathy. These are perceived capacities, not observed robot cognition/feeling or live home service. Reported mediation is statistical and correction-sensitive; original psychology sources are metadata-checked, not independently fully read.
access_limits: OSF raw data, scripts, item-level results, multiplicity family/q-values and manipulation-check participant flow were not independently reproduced.
The original cognitive/affective-ToM lesion paper, Cross robot-pain study and Batson chapter were checked for bibliographic identity only; no independent full-review credit.

The source explicitly acknowledges images/vignettes, a single severe harm narrative, no pre-existing trait baselines and no joint cToM×aToM manipulation. Those limitations remain part of the interpretation.

study.participants: Four recruited/retained main samples:1a90→81 (four attention and five comprehension exclusions),1b85→79 (three+three),2a145→120 (two+23),2b125→114 (four+seven). Total445 recruited/394 retained participations, not verified cross-experiment unique people. Main male/female counts29/52,23/56,40/80,25/89. Mean ages32.07,30.67,29.64,30.61. The first methods section dates collection to the first six months of2024; experiment-specific chronology is not fully supplied.
study.specificity_samples: The cognitive manipulation check explicitly recruits an additional40 participants; the affective specificity test also reports df38, but its distinct recruitment/overlap is not clearly specified. Do not fold these into a claimed total of independently verified unique participants or confuse them with the main outcome samples.
study.stimuli: Cognitive scenarios ask where an absent person will search after their apple/child has moved. High cToM reflects the person’s outdated belief; low gives the actual new location. Affective scenarios ask how someone feels after a desired apple is eaten or a child breaks a swimming promise: high says angry/disappointed, low happily excited. Thus affective level changes emotion valence/plausibility as well as attributed mentalizing; cognitive level also signals general competence.
study.procedure: After a service-robot introduction and a randomly assigned scenario, respondents imagine the owner pushing robot Neo from a bridge to stop a runaway tram and save a passerby; the robot is destroyed. A disassembled humanoid-robot image accompanies the harm. Experiments2 use home-service narratives, not live robot interaction. Robot-mind ratings precede the trauma/outcome in2, creating possible appraisal priming.
study.measures: Pain empathy: one1–10 item asking how painful the observer feels seeing Neo’s condition; it may mix vicarious pain with personal distress. Empathic concern: six1–7 adjectives, sympathy/softheartedness/warmth/compassion/tenderness/being moved, summed up to42, alpha.94–.95. Agency: morality, emotion recognition, self-control, memory, planning, communication; experience: happiness, fear, hunger, pain, anger, desire. These attributed capacities are not actual mental states or a pure objective performance test.
study.power: A-priori justification cites prior per-group samples20–36 rather than an explicit smallest-effect/alpha/power calculation. Later Monte Carlo mediation power is conditional on model parameters:2a .784 [.77,.80],2b1.000 [.999,1.000] and.839 [.83,.85]. Rounded1.000 is not certainty or independent evidence that all plausible effects are detectable.
study.specificity_results: Cognitive high/low cToM5.95(.83)/3.10(1.25), t38=−8.50, printed d=.53. Affective high/low aToM6.10(1.02)/2.50(1.10), t38=−10.73, printed d=.62. A20-per-arm pooled-SD reconstruction gives |d|≈2.69/3.39, respectively; the reported d labels/formulas need checking. Negative t can reflect reversed contrast order and is not itself inconsistent. Cross-dimension nulls do not establish selective manipulation equivalence.
study.direct_interaction: Authors do test a pooled experiment/type×level interaction, rather than only comparing significant versus nonsignificant arms: HC3 F1,156=3.48,p=.064 for pain and4.96,p=.027 for concern. Their statement that a significant interaction confirms the difference should be limited to concern at the reported unadjusted threshold. Type is confounded with separate experiment/scenario version and no joint within-study cToM×aToM factorial exists.
study.experiment2a: High/low cToM pain6.45(2.57)/6.77(2.49),t118=−.68,p=.498; experience14.53(7.15)/16.43(7.19),t118=−1.45,p=.151; concern29.58(8.86)/32.41(7.72),t118=−1.85,p=.066,d=−.34; agency30.88(6.03)/26.95(7.55),t118=3.17,p=.002,d=.58. Agency is higher in the high group, contrary to one sentence grouping it with the low-group concern tendency. The concern contrast is uncertain even before correction.
study.experiment2a_mediation: Agency indirect1.74,95%[.64,3.68]; direct−4.57[−7.49,−1.54], total−2.83, matching the group mean difference. Figure2 appears to show standardized .28/.37 paths, direct−.27,total−.17; these are not numerically interchangeable with unstandardized effects. Opposing paths can yield an uncertain total, but the mediator is not randomized and perceived threat/cunning is not measured.
study.experiment2b: High/low affective pain7.19(2.15)/6.18(2.43),t112=2.34,p=.021,d=.44; concern33.63(6.48)/28.36(9.12),Welch t96.77=3.53,p<.001,d=.67; experience24.85(9.69)/13.26(5.57),t93.74=7.90,p<.001,d=1.47; agency33.81(3.76)/22.98(6.27),t87.16=11.08,p<.001,d=2.09. The authors say pain fails their FDR correction while the others survive. Exact correction family/q-values are not supplied; preserve that qualification rather than treating rawp=.021 as robust replication.
study.experiment2b_mediation: A parallel model includes agency and experience. Experience indirect pain1.72[1.05,2.64], direct−.17[−1.40,1.08]; agency indirect CI[−1.61,.70]. Experience indirect concern3.18[.54,6.69],direct2.25[−2.23,7.32]; agency CI[−4.22,4.89]. Figure3 selectively displays experience paths and differently scaled coefficients. Because agency point estimates are omitted, experience+direct need not equal total; do not falsely declare the parallel model arithmetically impossible. Nonsignificant residual paths do not prove exact zero or sole causal mediation.
study.assumptions: Welch/HC3 handle reported heteroscedasticity;5000 bootstrap samples address indirect-effect sampling uncertainty. Nonnormal outcome-model residuals remain disclosed. Low VIF and bootstrapping do not establish linear-model correctness, no mediator confounding or causal validity. Screening mediation by total/mediator significance is inconsistently invoked across outcomes and should be justified.
study.scope: No real robot ToM, emotional suffering, actual helping, empathy physiology, long-term attachment, interface safety, babyface redesign efficacy or actual threat response is tested. Inference of another’s emotion, perceived capacity to infer, observer distress and other-oriented care are distinct. The authors themselves call the mediation exploratory and request live/varied contexts.

summary: Add affective theory of mind, pain empathy and empathic concern as distinct constructs with scope limits. Broaden the existing ToM umbrella definition to cover mental-state inference while retaining belief reasoning within it; do not add cognitive-ToM as a synonymous extra row. Enrich robot-directed empathy, agency/experience attribution and contagion boundaries. Correct the agency-direction sentence and qualify reported effect sizes, interactions, multiplicity and mediation without inventing causal certainty or raw-data fixes.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s emotional state from their situation and behavior, without necessarily sharing that emotion.
findings.novelty_rationale: Emotion-state inference differs from belief/location reasoning, attributing a capacity to feel, catching an expressed emotion or caring about another’s welfare. It is a component of the ToM umbrella rather than a synonym for all empathy.
findings.ai_evidence_status: The read experiments manipulate people’s perception that a fictional robot understands emotions. They do not validate an actual robot’s emotion inference or show that it shares feelings.
findings.ai_proposal: Test a model on context-rich emotion-inference tasks with plausible alternative interpretations, requesting calibrated uncertainty and checking whose emotion is being inferred. Hold expression valence and general competence constant in observer experiments; never treat fluent inference as proof of felt empathy.

evidence.quote: except the group difference in pain empathy.

findings.evidence_scope: The source distinguishes cognitive and affective ToM and uses angry/disappointed versus happily excited responses to manipulate perceived affective understanding. Empathic-concern differences are reported, while one pain contrast fails the stated correction. The original dissociation study is metadata-checked, not fully read.
findings.boundary: Understanding an emotion is not experiencing it. Situational cues can be ambiguous, and this valence/plausibility bundle does not uniquely validate a mentalizing mechanism. Perceived robot capacity, actual task performance, experience attribution and observer care are separate.

findings.definition: A vicarious affective response to another’s perceived pain or bodily harm.
findings.novelty_rationale: Pain-related resonance is distinct from a judgment about a target’s capacity to feel and from other-oriented empathic concern. Robot-directed empathy names the target domain, whereas pain empathy names the response dimension.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Humans report their own pain-related response to a fictional robot’s destruction; no model or robot felt pain is demonstrated.
findings.ai_proposal: For model outputs, evaluate sensitivity to described human pain and appropriate grounded support without claiming internal suffering or verifying a fictional robot’s sentience. In observer studies, measure vicarious pain separately from personal distress, sympathy and beliefs about the target’s actual sensations.

evidence.quote: robot Neo, how painful do you feel?
except the group difference in pain empathy.

findings.evidence_scope: A one-item observer rating increases under high affective-ToM descriptions in1b; in2b its rawp=.021 does not survive the authors’ reported FDR correction. Cognitive-ToM contrasts are uncertain. This measure may mix personal distress with vicarious pain and does not prove genuine pain in the robot.
findings.boundary: Apparent injury can evoke a response even when subjective pain in the target is unverified. One self-report is not a validated diagnosis, actual helping or an AI feeling. Keep source correction, scale limits and other-oriented care distinct.

findings.definition: Other-oriented feelings of sympathy, compassion and care for another’s welfare.
findings.novelty_rationale: Concern for another is distinct from sharing their pain, inferring their emotions, feeling one’s own distress or attributing a mind. It can occur toward humans or robots; the existing robot-directed umbrella does not separately name this response dimension.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human concern ratings toward a fictional damaged robot are measured. A model can display care-oriented behavior without that establishing a subjective compassionate state.
findings.ai_proposal: Assess whether an assistant recognizes a person’s relevant welfare needs and offers proportionate, accurate support, separately from emotional mirroring or unwarranted agreement. Measure observer-rated care and actual helpfulness without inferring a model’s inner feelings.

evidence.quote: warm, compassionate, tender, and being moved.

findings.evidence_scope: Six adjective items measure immediate concern toward Neo. High affective-ToM conditions show higher concern; cognitive-ToM has null/uncertain total contrasts and an exploratory opposing-path decomposition through agency. The source does not measure actual altruistic helping. Batson 1987 is a cited chapter, not independently fully read here.
findings.boundary: Concern is not necessarily beneficial action, correct judgment or proof that its target has subjective experiences. Warm ratings, pain resonance and emotional-state inference are distinct. Do not turn an unrandomized indirect path into a unique causal explanation.

findings.definition: Modelling others' beliefs; emerges partially in LLMs (npj AI 2025; Strachan 2024).
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the existing concept and add exact evidence/measurement boundaries rather than a duplicate label.
findings.evidence_scope: The read source distinguishes belief/intent inference from emotional-state inference and measures observers’ perception of those capacities in scripted robot responses. It does not test actual robot mentalizing, nor does its third-party task directly validate recursive second-order mentalizing about the observer.
findings.boundary: Separate genuine task ability, perceived ability, experience attribution and felt empathy. A correct-looking scripted answer can bundle competence, plausibility and emotion valence; it is not evidence of self-awareness or consciousness.
findings.previous_definition: Modelling others' beliefs; emerges partially in LLMs (npj AI 2025; Strachan 2024).
findings.revised_definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.definition_revision_reason: The existing umbrella name includes mentalizing but its definition was limited to beliefs and mixed the definition with an empirical LLM claim. The read source explicitly covers emotions, thoughts, intentions and desires. Clarify the neutral construct and retain individual AI evidence in source-specific notes; cognitive belief reasoning remains represented here.

findings.definition: An emotional response oriented toward a robot's apparent distress, pain or other experienced state.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the existing concept and add exact evidence/measurement boundaries rather than a duplicate label.

evidence.quote: pain empathy and empathic concern regarding
except the group difference in pain empathy.

findings.evidence_scope: Four vignette experiments separate pain-related observer ratings and six-item concern ratings after one severe fictional robot-destruction scenario. Affective-ToM descriptions generally raise concern, but the2b pain comparison fails the reported multiplicity correction and cognitive total effects are uncertain.
findings.boundary: A description/image is not actual robot suffering or real service interaction. Observer affect, concern, helping behavior and genuine machine mentality differ; statistical indirect effects do not uniquely identify causal pathways.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the existing concept and add exact evidence/measurement boundaries rather than a duplicate label.
findings.evidence_scope: Six-item agency appraisals are higher for high cognitive-ToM in2a and strongly higher for high affective-ToM in2b. In2a an exploratory positive indirect association through agency coexists with a negative adjusted path and an uncertain total concern contrast.
findings.boundary: Agency ratings include morality, memory, planning, communication and emotion recognition, not a pure isolated skill. A measured mediator is not randomized; positive indirect association does not establish a sole causal mechanism or real intention.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the existing concept and add exact evidence/measurement boundaries rather than a duplicate label.

evidence.quote: happiness, fear, hunger, pain, anger, and desire.
of the indirect effect of experience did not include zero

findings.evidence_scope: The experience scale asks happiness, fear, hunger, pain, anger and desire. High affective-ToM descriptions raise these ratings in2b; parallel mediation reports positive experience indirect associations with pain/concern while agency intervals include zero.
findings.boundary: Attributing a capacity to feel is distinct from inferring someone else’s emotion, observer concern and actual robot experience. A nonsignificant alternative path is not equivalence or proof of a unique causal mediator.

findings.definition: Catching the user's affect and mirroring it back.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the existing concept and add exact evidence/measurement boundaries rather than a duplicate label.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the introduction distinguishes emotional contagion from more complex pain/concern responses. The robot’s emotion-inference statement, target harm and observer ratings do not independently isolate catching and mirroring an expressed emotion.
findings.boundary: Do not label every emotional response to a damaged robot contagion. Shared valence, inferred distress, personal discomfort and other-oriented concern need separate measurements.

source_corrections.source_claim: The sentence says stronger concern and agency toward the low-cToM robot.
source_corrections.correction: Agency means30.88 high versus26.95 low indicate the opposite direction: high cToM has higher agency. Concern means29.58 high versus32.41 low trend toward greater low-group concern but p=.066 is not conventionally significant. Do not merge their direction or significance.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied text, means, tests and figures; raw output not reproduced.

source_corrections.source_claim: Printed d=.53 and.62 alongside40-person t tests and the reported means/SDs.
source_corrections.correction: Conventional equal20-per-arm pooled-SD reconstructions give |d|≈2.69 and3.39; t magnitudes8.50/10.73 agree with those larger standardized differences. The printed effect-size label/formula requires clarification. Do not replace raw values or infer a nonexistent participant split without the original output.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied text, means, tests and figures; raw output not reproduced.

source_corrections.source_claim: A significant experiment×condition interaction confirms the difference in empathy.
source_corrections.correction: The pooled concern interaction is p=.027; pain interaction is p=.064. Limit the stated significant differential pattern to concern at the reported threshold, and retain separate-experiment/multiplicity limitations.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied text, means, tests and figures; raw output not reproduced.

source_corrections.source_claim: High affective ToM consistently/significantly enhances both pain empathy and concern.
source_corrections.correction: Experiment2b explicitly says the pain difference and aToM–pain correlation do not survive FDR correction. Preserve that result; the concern effect is stronger. Exact correction family/q-values require code, so no alternative correction is invented.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied text, means, tests and figures; raw output not reproduced.

source_corrections.location: References to real service contexts, throughout
source_corrections.source_claim: Experiment2 described as a real home service setting.
source_corrections.correction: It uses home-service narratives and robot images. The limitations explicitly call for actual robots/video/field studies. Use realistic home-service vignettes rather than implying observed live encounters.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied text, means, tests and figures; raw output not reproduced.

methodological_limits: Text/image vignettes do not establish genuine robot mental capacities, a live service encounter or actual pain. Emotion plausibility/valence and competence vary with ToM level; no orthogonal control isolates the unique perception mechanism.

Post-assignment attention/comprehension exclusions, especially23 in2a, can condition on responses to the stimuli. Per-condition flow and sensitivity including failures are needed; random assignment alone does not resolve selected-sample bias.

Separate cognitive/affective experiments are not a randomized manipulation of both dimensions in the same factorial design. A direct pooled interaction is reported, but only concern reaches the stated threshold; pain p=.064 is not conventionally significant.

The one-item pain measure can reflect the observer’s own distress, while concern is an adjective-based emotional report. Neither establishes actual robot suffering, altruistic helping or stable trait empathy.

Correction family/q-values and nonsignificant-dimension estimates are absent. Treat the authors’ FDR qualification as part of the result, not an inconvenient detail to omit; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or selectivity.

Mediators are measured rather than randomized. Statistical direct/indirect decomposition, bootstrap intervals, residual checks and low VIF do not uniquely identify threat, experience or agency as causal pathways.

Conditional Monte Carlo power is not prospective proof of general adequacy. Reported manipulation-check d values need formula/output reconciliation; negative contrasts, scaled paths and omitted parallel mediator estimates are not automatically errors.

Original raw data/code and cited originals were not independently reproduced/read. Reported figure/scale information is preserved with uncertainty, and proposed design/marketing interventions remain unvalidated.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Robot/machine label work separates agency attribution from experience and actual mentality. Here affective descriptions raise both attributed dimensions, so construct selectivity and causal mediation cannot be assumed.

MindMiner could not reliably separate agency from experience in its text data. The current separate scales help specify dimensions, but correlated appraisals and nonrandom mediators still do not prove distinct causal mechanisms.

The judicial paper likewise has a small/uncertain total alongside an indirect association. Lack of total significance does not forbid mediation, while a positive indirect estimate does not establish an experimentally identified psychological process.

deferred.term: Cognitive theory of mind / first-order mentalizing
deferred.reason: Belief inference is already central to the existing ToM/mentalizing entry. Record the component distinction there rather than add another overlapping cognitive label.

The discussion invokes reasoning about how another views one’s own mind, but the scenarios mostly concern third-party beliefs/emotions. No direct validation of a separate recursive self-model is demonstrated; retain as an untested theoretical interpretation.
Cunning, threat, vulnerability and infant-schema explanations are conjectures; actual threat, strategic manipulation or babyface mediation is not measured.
Existing concept, discussed as an explanation but no actual reciprocal helping is measured here. Do not treat warmth/concern ratings as a new reciprocity experiment.

limitations: All 15 supplied pages, four tables and three figures were read. Original-source metadata checks do not imply full reading of the cited lesion study, robot-neuroscience paper or Batson chapter.
The results concern perceptions and self-reports, not proof of machine emotions, model consciousness or a recommendation to mislead users about those capacities.

source_identity_checks.finding: Crossref confirms all four authors and online29 December 2025. Creation metadata from November does not establish an earlier journal publication or correction.

The cognitive/affective-ToM source is Dissociable prefrontal networks for cognitive and affective theory of mind: A lesion study, Neuropsychologia45:3054–3067, DOI10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2007.05.021. Identity only; original full text not read.
The pain-empathy original is a Philosophical Transactions B374 article20180034, DOI10.1098/rstb.2018.0034. Identity only, not an independent full review.

Prosocial Motivation: Is it ever Truly Altruistic? is a chapter in Advances in Experimental Social Psychology20:65–122, DOI10.1016/S0065-2601(08)60412-8. The08 identifier does not make it a2008 empirical paper. Original chapter not read.

interpretation_qualifications.qualification: Scaled diagram paths and unstandardized bootstrapped effects differ. The parallel model includes an agency indirect path whose point estimate is not displayed, so direct+experience alone need not equal total. Preserve this plausible reconciliation instead of falsely flagging a sum inconsistency.

An indirect association can exist with a nonsignificant total effect; screening on total significance is not required. Conversely, bootstrap significance and low VIF do not establish causal mediation or zero residual effect.

Inferring another’s emotion is distinct from sharing that feeling. The source sometimes describes aToM in experiential language; the catalogue definition preserves inference rather than conflating it with affective empathy or actual robot sensations.
